entryAnswer.explanation:
What the adapter does. `mountSpendingDisplay` takes an already-created `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback, subscribes to each of the view's five business ports (`assessment`, `publication`, `coverage`, `issues`, `startup` — the exact keys of the frozen view object at examples/spending-alerts/causal-preset.ts:171-177), and calls `render` with the current values plus an explicit `unavailable` list. It never constructs a graph, node, resource, capability or input fact; the view is the caller's original object (README.md:91-96).

Value semantics. `Node.subscribe` is push-on-subscribe: a new sink receives `START`, then cached `DATA` (or `DIRTY` if dirty) (packages/ts/src/node/node.ts:416-419, 445-458). The adapter therefore treats only `DATA` as a usable value, and on `INVALIDATE` or `ERROR` it deletes the stored value instead of keeping the stale one. That matches the documented meaning: "Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value" (README.md:138). `INVALIDATE` clears the node cache to SENTINEL, drops the replay ring and broadcasts downstream (packages/ts/src/node/node-output-runtime.ts:451-459), so a later `DATA` is a genuinely new occurrence, not a replay of the old one. `START`, `DIRTY`, `RESOLVED`, `COMPLETE` and `TEARDOWN` carry no new usable value and are ignored for display; `RESOLVED` in particular is an undirty balance signal, not a value (node-output-runtime.ts:178-181).

What "a value becoming unavailable" means. It is a per-port fact about the current graph state: the port has no current usable value, so the display must show it as unavailable rather than as the last value. It is not a statement that the run ended, that the instance stopped, or that an outstanding obligation was recovered. The five latest port values are explicitly not an atomic multi-port snapshot (README.md:142; causal-view-binding.ts:9-13), so the observation is a set of independent latest values, and a missing publication does not mean no request was submitted (README.md:129-130).

What unmounting means. The returned cleanup function only ends observation: it unsubscribes every sink and is idempotent. Unsubscribing the last sink deactivates the node (node.ts:441-444), and deactivation clears compute caches and dep state (node-lifecycle-runtime.ts:76-102) — but it does not terminate the instance, release the resource, or cancel retained obligations. The README states this directly: "Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations" (README.md:143), and the application must preserve retained records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery (README.md:146-151). The adapter also does not call `runEndReady`/`inspect().normalEndReady`, which are readiness conditions, not proof of termination or release (README.md:144).

Boundaries. The adapter adds no business input facts and no new running instance; it does not reimplement view creation (task.json instructions; README.md:39-44). It also does not use the public `subscribeNodeValues` adapter, which ignores INVALIDATE and is not a substitute for this view contract (README.md:159-161).
